# The One Big Idea {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

When you "talk to AI," you talk to **two things**

## Why Start Here? {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="why" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
Understand *how* it works and you'll know **what to trust**, **what to check**, and
**how to get better answers**.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 1em;"}
Everything else today hangs off one insight: you're talking to **two layers stacked

:::

# The Model Layer {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

The brain in a jar

## A Brilliant Brain — With Amnesia {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="brain" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
A brilliant graduate's brain floating in a **jar**. It has read most of the internet,
so it's clever — but it has **total amnesia**.
:::

. . .

::: {.incremental}
- Knows nothing about *you*, your department, or what you said five minutes ago
- The instant it finishes answering, it **forgets everything**
- All it does is **predict the next word** from the text it was just handed
:::

## It Just Predicts the Next Word {auto-animate=true}

Under the hood it does **one** thing: guess the **next word** based on probability.

::: {data-id="predict" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 0.7em 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C; margin: 0.5em 0;"}
*"The capital of Saudi Arabia is…"*
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.95em;"}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
- **Riyadh** (99.8%) ✅
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
- Jeddah (0.1%) · Paris (0.00001%)
:::
:::

. . .

It doesn't *"know"* geography — it knows **"Riyadh" almost always follows that sentence.**

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
It does this *even when it has no idea* — the next slide.
:::

## When It Guesses Wrong (Hallucinations) {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="font-size: 1.1em; margin-bottom: 1em;"}
What happens when it doesn't know the answer? **It guesses.**
:::

"According to Article 214 of the new Saudi Investment Law: ..."

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
- **The** (45%)
- **Foreign** (30%)
- **Capital** (15%)
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C; margin-top: 1em;"}
The AI constructs a sentence that *sounds* legal, but it has never read the actual document.
:::

## The Limit That Explains Everything {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em;"}
The model is **stateless**. It does not "remember" and it does not "look things up."
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-important}
## This is why it "hallucinates"
When it doesn't know, it predicts a **plausible-sounding** answer anyway — a confident,
made-up citation, a journal that doesn't exist, a wrong date.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
Anything you want it to "know," you must **hand it every single time**.
:::

# The App Layer {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The office around the brain

## We Build an Office {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="office" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
The brain in a jar can't open files or remember your name. So we build an **office**
around it: filing cabinets, a notebook, a standing to-do list.
:::

. . .

Every time you ask for something, the office **gathers the relevant pages and hands
them to the brain** along with your request — then files the answer back.

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
The brain still has amnesia. The *office* is what makes it feel like it remembers.
:::

## The Sentence to Remember {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #00C9A7; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em;"}
The model **knows nothing and forgets everything**;
the app **re-sends what matters on every request.**
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## The features you've seen
"Memory," "Projects," "Custom Instructions" are all just the **app** gathering and
re-sending context for you. Cowork (later today) is a very capable office.
:::

# What "Context" Really Is {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

The pages on the brain's desk

## Context = the Desk {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="context" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
**Context** is everything stacked on the brain's desk before it starts — your request
**plus** the background pages it needs: your instructions, the paper you pasted, your rules.
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em; margin-top: 1em;"}
Output quality is mostly a **context problem**, not a **smartness problem.**
:::

## The Desk Has Limits {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="window" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
The desk has a **fixed size**. Pile on too much and **older pages fall off the edge** —
that's why a long chat starts forgetting how it began.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## The fix
**Saved instructions beat re-pasting.** The office puts the important pages back on the
desk for you every time — the foundation of the assistant you'll build today.
:::


# It All Clicks {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The payoff

## The Office Getting Smarter {auto-animate=true}

Everything you'll build today is just **the app deciding what to re-send**:

::: {.incremental}
- **Standing instructions** — your rules, re-sent every time
- **Memory** — facts about you, re-sent when relevant
- **Skill** — a saved recipe the app runs on command
- **Grounding** — your sources put on the desk, on purpose
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
None of it is magic. It's all **context management.**
:::

## Micro-Check {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The AI cites a journal article that **doesn't exist**. Which layer failed?

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #9B8EC0; color: white; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center;"}
**The Model Layer** — the brain **guessed**. Ground it in a real source and **verify**
(later, with NotebookLM).
:::
:::

# Stop Asking. Start Delegating. {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Now put the two layers to work — brief the AI like a teaching assistant

## The Shift {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="shift" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
You don't need a "chat bot." You need a **capable assistant** you can delegate to.
:::

. . .

::: {data-id="example" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7; margin-top: 1em;"}
**Don't ask:** "Write an email about the meeting."

**Delegate:** "Act as a thesis advisor. Draft a recap email to my student from these
notes. Highlight the revisions due before the next committee."
:::

# RICE {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

The 4 pillars of a good prompt

## The Framework {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="rice" style="font-size: 1.1em;"}

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**R — Role:** Who should the AI be?
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**I — Instructions:** What exactly should it do? (format, length, tone)
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**C — Context:** What information does it need?
:::
::: {.fragment .fade-in}
**E — Examples:** Show it what "good" looks like.
:::

:::

## R — Role {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="pillar" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.3em;"}
**Who** should the AI be?
:::

. . .

::: {.incremental}
- A patient teaching assistant
- A peer reviewer for a journal
- A curriculum committee chair
- A grant-proposal editor
:::

. . .

The role shapes the AI's vocabulary, perspective, and priorities.

## I — Instructions {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="pillar" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.3em;"}
**What** exactly should it do?
:::

. . .

Bundle the task **with** its format, length, and tone:

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
"Draft a **150-word** feedback note to the student. Encouraging but specific. Use a
bulleted 'What to fix next' list."
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pro move
Add: "If anything is unclear, **ask me before you write**."
:::

## C — Context {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="pillar" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.3em;"}
**What** information does it need?
:::

. . .

The "brain dump" — paste your notes, the rubric, the draft, the syllabus.

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## This is the *same* context from the two layers
You're loading the pages onto the brain's desk. **No context = the brain guesses.**
:::

## E — Examples {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="pillar" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.3em;"}
**Show** it what "good" looks like.
:::

. . .

Don't just *describe* the output — **paste one sample**. The AI copies its structure,
tone, and length.

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
"Match this style: *'Dear Sara, strong progress this week. Three things to tighten before
we meet: …'*"
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## One example beats a paragraph
A single sample teaches more than ten lines of rules.
:::

## The Formula {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #625D9C)"}

::: {style="background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.05em;"}
"Act as a **[Role]**. Your job is to **[Instructions]**. Here is the **[Context]**.
Match this **[Example]**."
:::

# Live Demo {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

Messy meeting notes → a clean student email

## The Messy Notes {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="story" style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
What you actually scribbled after the committee meeting:
:::

::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.82em; font-style: italic;"}
"Met Sara re: thesis ch.3. Stats section weak — needs effect sizes, not just p-values.
Lit review missing 2 key papers (ask her to add). Committee wants revised draft in 3 weeks.
She's nervous about the defense — reassure. Reminder: ethics form still not submitted."
:::

## The RICE Prompt {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.72em;"}
**Role:** Act as a supportive thesis advisor.

**Instructions:** Draft a warm, clear follow-up email to my student. Use headers —
Summary, Required Revisions, Deadline, Admin. Put the deadline in **bold**. End on an
encouraging note. If anything is missing, add a "Questions for me" section.

**Context:** Notes from today's committee meeting on Chapter 3: *[paste notes]*

**Example:** Match this opening — *"Dear Sara, good progress this week. Here's where we
landed: …"*
:::

## What Made It Work {auto-animate=true}

::: {.incremental}
- **Role** → wrote as a mentor, not a robot
- **Instructions** → clear sections + tone + the "Questions for me" rule
- **Context** → messy notes were enough — the AI extracted the structure
- **Example** → matched the warm, personal opening
:::

# When AI Fumbles a Hard Question {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

One move to trust the numbers

## Slow It Down — Especially on Numbers {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.05em;"}
By default AI answers **fast and shallow** — risky on grades, totals, and data.
:::

. . .

::: {data-id="dc" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
**Double-check:** have it solve the **same task 2–3 times** — match = trust, mismatch = flag.

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
*"Total these 40 exam scores three times. If all three match, output 'Verified'; if not,
'Manual Review Needed'."* — *industry term: **Self-Consistency**.*
:::
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #666; font-size: 0.9em; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
Two more nudges for harder calls: **"think step by step"** *(Chain of Thought — logic)* ·
**"debate it out"** *(Tree of Thoughts — judgment)*.
:::

## Key Takeaways {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Two layers** — the model (brain) and the app (office) stacked together
2. **The brain has amnesia** — stateless, predicts the next word, can hallucinate
3. **Quality is a context problem** — the right pages on the desk → the right answer
4. **Delegate, don't ask** — brief the AI with **RICE** (Role, Instructions, Context, Examples)
5. **Examples are the secret weapon**; slow it down on hard problems — step by step, debate it out, double-check
:::
